title: Urate–creatinine coupling did not improve cross-cycle handgrip prediction beyond flexible conventional biomarkers
abstract: A continuous urate–renal interaction was tested for incremental prediction of contemporaneous maximum handgrip, motivated by earlier urate–kidney–muscle associations. Source-only weighted ridge models in NHANES2011–2012 adults aged60+(n=1363) were transferred without refitting to independently recruited NHANES2013–2014 adults(n=1521). A flexible baseline included demographics, anthropometry, albumin, urate, creatinine and urate/creatinine. Adding a standardized log-urate by log-creatinine product changed target MSE from 28.986674 to 28.995054 kg². The gain was -0.008379, with300-refit survey-PSU bootstrap95% interval [-0.255577,0.187633]. Source cross-validation was also negative on average; sensitivity gains changed sign. We found no reliable increment for this feature. Cross-cycle validation is not independent-clinic validation, and neither causality nor absence of physiological interaction is established. Reproducible public-input provenance and AI author self-checks accompany this negative result.
